investigation.title: Remote Agent Creation Eval Failing: Swarm Gateway 502 on POST /api/agents (production-api)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-08-31T03:40–41Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error indicating the swarm gateway ELB endpoint was unreachable during agent provisioning. Because the failure occurs at the very first HTTP call to POST /api/agents — before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) can be collected — every required contract assertion is unmet and the eval cannot progress past the gateway boundary.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway (an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning path) was unreachable at the time of the eval run. The production-api layer returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This is an infrastructure-layer failure at the swarm gateway, not a code defect in the eval runner or contract definitions. All three sibling checks share the identical error message, confirming a single shared upstream dependency — the swarm gateway — is the point of failure rather than any individual check's logic.

investigations.rootCause: The AURA backend was temporarily unable to reach the upstream model provider for aura-gpt-5-5 at the time of the eval run (2026-08-31T03:40:05–18Z). This is an issue on our side, not with your account or credits." This is an upstream provider connectivity or availability fault surfaced through AURA's runtime harness, not an eval infrastructure defect. investigations.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocking All Remote Agent Provisioning Evals (remote-agents / production-api)
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-runtime, remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state) failed at 2026-08-31T03:40–03:41Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api layer could not reach the swarm ELB endpoint at /v1/agents. Because agent provisioning is the first step in every remote-agents eval, no check was able to produce any evidence, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) is entirely unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The swarm gateway — an AWS ELB in us-east-2 fronting the /v1/agents provisioning endpoint — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. Every remote-agents check calls POST /api/agents as its first step (evidenced by the createAgent call at run-status-probes.mjs line 1918), and all three returned the same error body ("swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning", code: bad_gateway) within a ~22-second window, confirming a shared upstream dependency failure rather than an issue in any individual check's logic or expected-output contract. This is an eval-layer failure reflecting a real infrastructure connectivity problem; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet to confirm a broader production outage.

[Possible] A network routing or security-group change between the production-api and the swarm ELB blocked outbound connections to the ELB's HTTP endpoint, causing the gateway to return bad_gateway before any backend was reached.
[Possible] The swarm service behind the ELB crashed or was restarting (e.g., a deployment), making the ELB return 502 because no healthy targets were available to handle /v1/agents requests.

[Less likely] A transient DNS or load-balancer health-check misconfiguration caused a brief window of unavailability that happened to coincide with the scheduled eval run — this would be self-healing and may not recur.
